3. [RLOW.14.3] **Compiler-emitted terminal ordering.** The
   firing-priority total order's FIRST key is the
   terminal ordinal ([LDET.5.4]). The compiler must emit
   terminals in a canonical source order the agenda can
   read back, and the encoding is not an implementation
   choice: earlier in its source file first, and across
   files **import-DAG topological, leaf libraries first**,
   so libraries come before the files that import them.

   The oracle rules the compiler synthesizes for tests ([RTIM.14.11]) are
   outside that source order. The compiler **must** emit every oracle rule's
   terminal after every other terminal in the artefact, whichever module's test
   it serves, in ascending `test_id` ([RLOW.17.1]) and then ascending assertion
   position, the `<t>` and `<i>` of its name ([RTIM.14.13]). Every other rule
   then has the same ordinal whether or not the artefact carries tests.
